text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - Britain's FTSE 100 index ended lower after reversing opening gains into new high ground and running out of steam following a hefty four percent rise the previous four sessions. UK equities had looked to Wall Street for fresh incentive to push higher but an unsteady start in New York dragged the FTSE back to the worst level of the day.
The FTSE 100 finished 14.8 points off at 4,724.8 after setting a new peakof 4,759.3.

FRANKFURT - German shares notched up modest gains in bourse trade as the market drew some strength from overnight gains on Wall Street and placed uncertainty about monetary union on the backburner. The blue chip DAX index advanced 12.42 points to close the floor session at 3,677.43 points. In post-bourse trade the index rose 0.71 to 3,671.87.
PARIS - French shares closed higher on Wednesday but off the day's highs after a late interruption in trade caused by a storm. The CAC-40 index finished up 32.01 points at 2,696.19.
ZURICH - Swiss shares ended one percent down, continuing Tuesday's consolidation, as derivatives-related selling and the easing dollar put pressure on some high-profile Swiss stocks.
Dealers said investors have grown cautions following a five-day bull run on the Swiss bourse, but fundamentals were seen as favourable. The SMI ended down 53.3 points at 5,308.6.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks fell due to worries that the yen's recent rally against the dollar may continue and hurt the competitiveness of export-oriented issues, brokers said. The Nikkei average shed 242.62 points to finish at 20,289.93.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed slightly lower after a day of big price swings as profit-taking alternated with bargain-hunting, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index ended 18.19 points lower at 14,421.52.
SYDNEY - The Australian stock market eased off its record breaking run as investors booked profits.

Brokers said a large portfolio went through the market, boosting trade in a see-saw session. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,613.7 points, down 15.2 points from Tuesday's record close and off the fresh intra-day high of 2,635.7 hit earlier in the day.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended slightly firm after retracing early losses sparked by some profit-taking but Amplat's move to merge its operations stole the limelight. Amplat's Lebowa Platinum Ltd finished up 110 cents at 440 cents following Amplats' announcement on Tuesday that all its operation would now be put in Rusplats .

The market which failed to take a cue from Wall Street's climb overnight was also buoyed by U.S. agency Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co's move to assign an investment grade BBB minus rating to the country's foreign currency obligations. The industrial index ended up 3.3 points to 8,504.7, the gold index was down 12.8 points to 1,164.5 and the all-share index gained 20.6 points to 7,286.1.
